answers.answer: In bt_scheduler_core/scheduler.py start(), after run creation or binding verification, start() calls _plan_all_routes() before reconciliation and dispatch. In _plan_all_routes(), it constructs a PlanRoutingRequest containing every task in self.plan.tasks wrapped in TaskView, which includes all tasks in the approved DAG, including pending and blocked tasks waiting on prerequisites (dependencies=spec.after), not only READY tasks.

The concrete bridge from Scheduler adapter to M2 is PlanRoutingPort.plan implemented in bt_scheduler_adapter.py and bt_scheduler_plan_routing.py plan_full_dag. It performs one batch operation for the entire map rather than one decision per task: plan_full_dag maps all tasks into a tuple of DecisionRequest objects, and executes a single port.ledger.batch_decisions.persist() call, which invokes M2's plan_ready_batch joint allocation algorithm.

Planned routes and unavailable reasons are persisted in M1's RunState (schema 2) under each TaskRec (fields route_metadata, route_status, route_reason) via a state transaction in _plan_all_routes(), with an audit entry plan_routes_received. Repeating the map on restart is prevented by the boolean flag ctx.state.routing_complete, which is set to True upon completion and checked at the beginning of _plan_all_routes().

Whole-plan mapping does not reserve executor capacity or launch work; planned routes are non-reserving advisory recommendations. Actual capacity and resource reservation is performed strictly inside M1 by reservation.claim() (invoked via SchedulerCore.claim() during _assign()), which verifies free slots and resource conflicts, creates an AttemptRec in state RESERVED, places holds on resources, marks the task route_status as assigned, and writes a start order to the outbox.

The old planned model/profile is not blindly reused. During step(), when tasks become READY and slots are free, _assign() invokes the assignment port propose(AssignmentRequest). SchedulerAdapter.propose refreshes live account quota via refresh_quota_preflight, recalculates candidate status (marking non-available providers as unknown), and invokes batch_decisions.persist and engine.decide to dynamically re-evaluate and assign the best eligible route under the fresh quota conditions.

In bt_scheduler_adapter.py (lines 357-359) and bt_scheduler_plan_routing.py (lines 147-150), an exception from refresh_quota_preflight is caught and converted to {"*": {"status": "unavailable", "reason": "quota_refresh_failed"}}, which causes _apply_preflight and propose to mark candidates as unknown and evidence as refresh_failed. In bt_scheduler_plan_routing.py, quota_aware_requested_at() computes requested_at as max(initial_time, time.time(), observed_at), preventing the request timestamp from preceding any fresh observation timestamp returned by the refresh.

In bt_scheduler_core/tests/test_routing.py, test_full_dag_is_recorded_then_ready_route_is_revalidated_without_executor tests this scenario. It sets up 3 tasks (T1 ready, T2 blocked on T1, T3 independent). On start(), M2 plan() recommends sonnet xhigh for all 3 tasks (recorded as recommended, routing_complete=True) without execution port or reservations. On step(), M1 revalidates READY tasks (T1, T3) via propose(), assigning T1 to haiku low, leaving blocked T2 as recommended sonnet, and creating exactly 1 pending outbox start order.
